name: Cornwall

neighbourhoods.name: Truro
neighbourhoods.housing: A small cathedral city of Georgian townhouses, Victorian terraces and modern estates on the edges.

neighbourhoods.name: Falmouth
neighbourhoods.housing: Harbour town of Victorian terraces and townhouses, with many student lets for Falmouth University.

neighbourhoods.name: Newquay
neighbourhoods.housing: A resort town of guest houses, holiday flats, terraces and modern apartment blocks.

neighbourhoods.name: Camborne and Redruth
neighbourhoods.housing: Former mining towns with granite and brick terraces and post-war estates.

neighbourhoods.name: Penzance
neighbourhoods.housing: Victorian and Georgian terraces and granite houses around the harbour and seafront.

neighbourhoods.name: St Ives
neighbourhoods.housing: Fishermen's cottages and holiday lets on steep narrow streets.

neighbourhoods.name: St Austell
neighbourhoods.housing: A former china clay town of terraces, post-war estates and newer housing.

neighbourhoods.name: Bodmin
neighbourhoods.housing: A market town of Victorian terraces and large modern estates.

neighbourhoods.name: Saltash
neighbourhoods.housing: A commuter town for Plymouth with terraces and modern estates above the Tamar.

neighbourhoods.name: Bude
neighbourhoods.housing: A seaside town of Victorian houses, bungalows and holiday homes.

housing: Cornwall's housing ranges from granite and slate cottages in fishing villages to Victorian mining-town terraces and large post-war and modern estates around Truro, St Austell, Bodmin and Camborne. Holiday lets and second homes are a big part of the market in coastal towns such as St Ives, Padstow and Newquay, which squeezes long-term private renting. Falmouth and Penryn have many student lets for Falmouth University. Many rural homes are off the gas grid, with oil, LPG or electric heating, and solid-walled stone houses are prone to damp.
checkinTips: Granite and stone cottages: photograph solid walls and window reveals for damp and mould, and the condition of slate roofs visible from outside.
Off-grid homes: record the oil tank or LPG gauge reading, the boiler, any septic tank or private water supply, and wood burner condition.
Coastal properties: look for salt corrosion on window frames, door furniture, gates and outdoor lights, and wind damage to fences.
Student lets in Falmouth and Penryn: photograph each bedroom's lock and furniture and the shared kitchen and bathroom separately.
Former mining areas around Camborne and Redruth: note any cracks in walls so ground movement can be compared later.
Homes switched from holiday let to long-term let: list furniture, linen and kitchen items carefully, as inventories often change.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair or unsafe conditions in a private rented home can contact Cornwall Council's private sector housing team, which can inspect and enforce standards.
